content:
jamal: FYI prepping a Redwood Private (VPC) rollout for a customer that requires KMS for control-plane + data-plane. Quick q: do we standardize on customer-owned CMKs in their account or support Redwood-managed cross-account keys? Need a short runbook for the solutions/SEs.

maria: short answer: prefer customer-owned CMKs in the customer's AWS account for Private. Reasons: least-privilege, audit visibility in their CloudTrail, legal/data residency. Redwood gets cross-account grants to operate. :white_check_mark:

alex: agreed. Customer-kept CMKs gives them audit + full control (rotation, policies). For customers that can't manage keys we can offer Redwood-managed CMKs as an option but mark it as higher trust.

jamal: good. For control-plane (secrets/config) vs data-plane (payload/model cache blobs) any nuance?

maria: yes. Control-plane secrets: encrypt at rest with customer's CMK (KEK) and store ciphertext in our control-plane DB. Data-plane: envelope encryption model — each DEK per blob/session. DEKs get generated locally by the service and encrypted under the customer's CMK. We keep only the ciphertext and cached plaintext DEK in memory for TTL.

alex: implementation notes / commands you can paste into the runbook:
```bash
# create a CMK in customer account (example)
aws kms create-key --description "Redwood Private control-plane CMK for ACME" --tags TagKey=Owner,TagValue=ACME
aws kms create-alias --target-key-id <key-id> --alias-name alias/redwood-private-acme

# grant Redwood control-plane role permission (one-time admin action in customer account)
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/redwood-private-acme \
  --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-controlplane \
  --operations Encrypt Decrypt ReEncryptFrom ReEncryptTo GenerateDataKey GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext DescribeKey
```

maria: important policy notes: include the Redwood role ARNs in the key policy or a KMS grant. Example key policy snippet (customer account):
```json
{
  "Sid": "AllowRedwoodControlPlane",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-controlplane"},
  "Action": ["kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:Decrypt","kms:ReEncrypt*","kms:DescribeKey"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```

alex: note on grants vs policies: grants are faster at server-side because they avoid extra policy evaluation on each call and are recommended for high QPS operations (GenerateDataKey). Grants can be restricted by operations and time-to-live. Good approach: key policy allows Redwood to call CreateGrant, then ops team creates a granular grant per role.

jamal: rotation — how do we handle CMK rotation and rewrap of existing DEKs? Customer may enable automatic yearly rotation.

maria: two options:
- If CMK auto-rotation is enabled (symmetric keys), future GenerateDataKey calls will use current key version; existing ciphertext remains under old key material. To re-encrypt stored DEKs to the new CMK material without exposing plaintext, run a rewrap job that calls ReEncrypt:
```bash
aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://dek-ciphertext.bin --destination-key-id alias/new-cmk --source-encryption-context '{}' --destination-encryption-context '{}'
```
This converts ciphertext to be under the new key without plaintext exposure.
- Alternatively, Decrypt -> GenerateDataKey (new CMK) -> re-encrypt DEK. ReEncrypt is preferable to avoid exposing plaintext in transit/storage.

alex: also watch DEK cache TTLs. If you keep plaintext DEKs cached long enough, rotation needs to flush caches and force rewraps. Add a cache-coherency step: upon rewrap, push an invalidate webhook to data-plane nodes so they fetch the rewrapped DEK (or re-run GenerateDataKey flow).

jamal: audit requirements: what do we log?

maria: customer CloudTrail will show KMS usage (Encrypt, Decrypt, GenerateDataKey, CreateGrant, ReEncrypt). We should additionally emit internal audit events: which Redwood principal used the key, operation context (control-plane vs data-plane, resource id), and correlation id. Store minimal metadata only — never persist plaintext DEKs.

alex: misc operational tips:
- Prefer symmetric KMS keys for these flows. Asymmetric keys don't support GenerateDataKey.
- For very strict customers, support external key stores (AWS EKS/EKS EKM) or CloudHSM-backed keys, but note higher latency.
- For cross-region DR, recommend multi-region replica keys and a rewrap plan that targets region-key aliases.

jamal: any perf caveats? We need low latency for data-plane lookups (model cache).

maria: generate DEK locally once with GenerateDataKey, cache plaintext DEK in memory (encrypted long-term). Use grants to avoid IAM policy eval at call time. Use batch-encrypt patterns where possible (bulk GenerateDataKey) for throughput. Monitor KMS throttling metrics and set fallback policies (local ephemeral keys) if KMS is unavailable — but that needs customer approval.

alex: security edge cases:
- Ensure key policy forbids KMS:DisableKeyRotation by default (so customer can control).
- For BYOK / external keys, clarify we only request necessary permissions.
- Rotate grants monthly as hygiene (revoke + recreate) if customer wants short-lived grants.

jamal: thanks. I'll draft the runbook + checklists. Action items: jamal -> draft runbook; maria -> produce key policy + grant templates; alex -> prototype rewrap job + cache-invalidation webhook.

sre-bot: deploy-checklist created: https://redwood-internal/ops/runbooks/kms-private-acme (placeholder) :robot_face:

jamal: awesome. tagging @maria @alex will sync tomorrow to review the runbook and the CLI snippets. :slightly_smiling_face:
